newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MOTOR RALLYING-WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN FAVOURITE FOR SWEDEN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RALLYING-WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN FAVOURITE FOR SWEDEN.

text.p: - Finn Tommi Makinen will start the Swedish Rally, which begins with a stage on a frozen river in Karlstad on Friday evening, with high hopes of completing a hat-trick of Swedish victories for his Mitsubishi team.
The reigning world champion, who started his successful 1996 campaign with victory in Sweden 12 months ago, finished second here in 1995 behind Kenneth Eriksson.
He says this year's rally will give him the perfect chance to outpace his title rivals, Briton Colin McRae and Spaniard Carlos Sainz.

"This is one of my favourite rallies and it has some good memories for me," said the 32-year-old Makinen, who finished third in Monte Carlo two weeks ago. "Our new car is very easy to drive and I think we can have a really good event here."

Italian Piero Liatti, the winner of the season-opening Monte Carlo rally for his Subaru team, has only a limited programme this year and will be absent from Sweden. His place will be taken by Eriksson, the home favourite.

"We will have completed three tests before the rally starts and it's a busy time for us as we try to find out the best tyres," Eriksson said. "But at least we will have an advantage as it is second nature for me to make judgements about the ground conditions here."
The weather is likely to play a major factor in the outcome of the rally, with mild weather leaving much of the rally's route bare of the usual deep snow.
The four-day rally takes place in the Varmland and Dalarma regions of the country, with 24 special stages.
